title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: this is Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' draft on a combinatorial, tame topology of one-dimensional figures. M is a finite cellular decomposition of a line (or segment): points P_a and arcs, each arc with an origin or(·) and an extremity ex(·). A 'préfigure' (préforme) is a subset of M that defines a reasonable locally closed figure; 'figures' are the closed ones. A connected préfigure is essentially an interval, open or closed at each end.

The previous page sets up two relations:
- a positional order <_pos on M, extended to parts by Φ <_pos Ψ iff X < Y for all X in Φ and Y in Ψ;
- a strengthened relation Φ <^!_pos Ψ: Φ <_pos Ψ, and if ex(Φ) = or(Ψ) = a, then the vertex P_a lies in neither Φ nor Ψ.

This page states what the extra condition is for. It excludes the 'recollés' (glued) case, where Φ and Ψ would not be open and closed in Φ ∪ Ψ, i.e. where their union would be connected rather than a disjoint union with Φ and Ψ as components.

Structure theorem for an arbitrary préfigure in terms of connected ones:
- Take a flag (chain) D = {Φ_1 <^! Φ_2 <^! ... <^! Φ_n} of connected préfigures, D ∈ Drap*_{<^!}(Préfig conn(M)).
- Associate to it Φ_D = ⋃ Φ_i, a disjoint union.
- The strengthened order is exactly what makes the Φ_i the connected components of Φ_D.
- Implicitly, D ↦ Φ_D is a bijection between such flags and all préfigures. This is the decomposition of a 1-dimensional constructible set into finitely many linearly ordered, separated intervals.

Lemma (completed on the next page): for connected préfigures Φ, Ψ:
- Φ ∩ Ψ = ∅ and Φ ∪ Ψ is a préfigure iff Φ ≤_pos Ψ (or symmetrically Ψ ≤_pos Φ);
- they are moreover the connected components of the union iff Φ <^! Ψ or Ψ <^! Φ, i.e. {Φ, Ψ} is a <^!-flag.

Page 100 then reparametrises préfigures by pairs (flag D in a poset L, subset α of the boundary ∂D) as F_D minus α.
errors: No mathematical error. Some statements are elliptical. The lemma as written gives only Φ ≤_pos Ψ, but the symmetric alternative (or Ψ ≤_pos Φ) is needed; it is supplied on the next page.
The insertion 'il pas' should make the sentence read 'on exclut le cas où Φ, Ψ ne seraient pas des parties ouvertes et fermées de Φ∪Ψ'. Without the negation the sentence is inverted.

ideas.what: Strengthened positional order <^! that forbids gluing at a shared endpoint, so that the ordered pieces are clopen in their union.
ideas.modern_name: Separation condition for connected components of a 1-dimensional constructible/definable set (cell decomposition on a line).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; formalised in o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s).
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs manuscripts; Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces 'topologie modérée' in general terms.

ideas.what: Bijection between flags (chains) of connected préfigures under <^! and arbitrary préfigures, via disjoint union, with the flag members being exactly the connected components.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of a finite union of intervals into its ordered connected components.

ideas.what: Lemma: two connected préfigures are disjoint with union a préfigure iff they are position-comparable; they are the components of the union iff <^!-comparable.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but elementary combinatorial bookkeeping step: connected components of a constructible subset of a cellular line, encoded as flags. It belongs to Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, but the content itself is standard and contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The flag relation is the strengthened order <^! (exclamation mark above), with 'pos' written beneath. It is not '≪^1'. The struck-through subscripts are 'pos' as well.
Inserted words in line 3: 'ne ... pas' ('ne seraient pas des parties ouvertes et fermées de Φ∪Ψ').
The text appears to read 'préfigure(s)' and 'Préfig conn(M)' (connexes), consistent with 'Préfig comm' on the next page. 'Préf conn' and 'préforme' are approximations.
Line after the union formula: probably '(réunion disjointe). C'est là le fait qu'il fallait pour que les Φ_i soient les composantes connexes de Φ_D'. The final symbol is Φ_D, not Φ.
End of lemma: 'il faut et suffit que Φ ≤_pos Ψ', followed by a struck 'Pour que Φ ...'.
